doc.title: Joe Darensbourg and Minor "Ram" Hall Interview, 1957-04-18

title: Playing little towns that had never heard jazz
summary: In small towns the troupe were big shots, like Ellington or Elvis, in places that had never heard a saxophone or organized jazz.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Play a little gig, huh? Yeah, we played the little towns, and believe it or not, I mean, uh, we, we, we, we, we, we, we were big shots when we hit those little towns. Yeah. That's, it was comparable of, uh, Duke Ellington or Elvis Presley coming to Los Angeles. Yeah.

It sounds fantastic now, but it's true. Yeah. They were all one to split. They wanted you to play. You, you, you, you, you was a big man when you hit one of those towns. Everybody wanted to see you. We played a little towns, like, uh, we played towns that guys had never heard a saxophone in person before. Never heard one. And the people in those little towns heard, heard much jazz before? No, no. Maybe once in a while. Some of the guys had left the town. We played towns that jazz had never come through, I mean organized.
